title: An atlas of cells in the human tonsil
summary: This is the reference atlas (Azimuth human_tonsil_v2). In the epithelial compartment the authors identified three clusters overlapping the keratinocyte populations of the oral mucosa; one of these expressed FDCSP and was annotated 'FDCSP epithelium'. The atlas notes FDCSP was first described in FDC and in leukocyte-infiltrated tonsillar crypts, with the specific crypt population previously unknown, and provides evidence that FDCSP-expressing cells are a specific subpopulation of the tonsillar epithelium. FDCSP and KRTDAP marker calls here are transcript-level (scRNA-seq / multiome), not protein-level. Tonsillar crypts and their lining subepithelial connective tissue septum are a recurring spatial niche in the atlas (e.g. tissue-resident CD8 T cells).
quotes: In the epithelial compartment, we identified three clusters overlapping with the keratinocyte populations of the oral mucosa (Figures S6A-S6C).
One of these clusters expressed FDCSP (FDCSP epithelium).
FDCSP was first described in FDC and in ''leukocyte-infiltrated tonsillar crypts,'' although the specific population within the crypts remained unknown.
Here, we provide evidence that FDSCP-expressing cells represent a specific subpopulation of the tonsillar epithelium.
Palatine tonsils are secondary lymphoid organs representing the first line of immunological defense against inhaled or ingested pathogens.

title: FDC-SP, a Novel Secreted Protein Expressed by Follicular Dendritic Cells
summary: Original identification of FDC-SP (FDCSP), the follicular dendritic cell secreted protein, from human reactive tonsils. Cited by the atlas as the source that first described FDCSP in FDC and in leukocyte-infiltrated tonsillar crypts. Establishes FDCSP as a small secreted protein of the immune system; expression here is protein/transcript in FDC, not epithelial. No body snippet retrieved beyond atlas citation context, so no verbatim quote is stored for this paper.

title: FDCSP Is an Immune-Associated Prognostic Biomarker in HPV-Positive Head and Neck Squamous Carcinoma
summary: Broader-literature context on FDCSP protein biology. Reports that among human normal tissues FDCSP shows its highest expression in tonsil tissue and gingival epithelium, and describes FDCSP as a small secreted protein originally discovered in follicular dendritic cells that specifically binds activated B cells and regulates antibody responses. Expression evidence is protein (IHC/immune) and BioGPS transcript-level; supports the plausibility of an FDCSP-high epithelial/tonsil niche but is a cancer study, not the tonsil atlas.
quotes: FDCSP showed the highest expression levels in tonsil tissue and gingival epithelium, with expression levels larger than 5 (raw data were downloaded from BioGPS).
FDCSP is expressed mostly by activated FDCs and TNF-alpha-activated FDC-like cell lines.
FDCSP specifically binds to activated B cells and functions as a regulator of antibody responses.

title: Multi-omics analysis identifies the unique high-FDCSP basal cells in triple-negative breast cancer
summary: Broader-literature context showing that in epithelial tissue FDCSP marks a basal-cell (rather than luminal) epithelial subpopulation, supporting the interpretation that FDCSP in the tonsil marks a specific epithelial subpopulation. FDCSP is described as a small secreted peptide with specific binding affinity to activated B cells. Expression evidence combines single-cell/spatial transcriptomics with IHC/IF (protein). This is a breast-cancer study, not tonsil-specific.
quotes: Single-cell transcriptome analysis demonstrated that FDCSP was predominantly highly expressed in basal cells but exhibited low expression in luminal epithelial cells.
FDCSP is a unique secreted peptide with a distinct expression pattern in the immune system and exhibits specific binding affinity to activated B cells.

title: Identification of novel follicular dendritic cell sarcoma markers, FDCSP and SRGN, by whole transcriptome sequencing
summary: Broader-literature context on FDCSP origin and function. States FDCSP was isolated in 2002 from human reactive tonsils and is specifically expressed by B-cell-activating FDC, and that studies suggest it can modulate the B-cell immune response and may have a role in autoimmune diseases. Provides functional grounding for FDCSP as an immune-modulatory secreted protein; expression here is protein (IHC) in FDC and FDC sarcoma, not epithelial.
quotes: FDCSP, isolated in 2002 from human reactive tonsils, is specifically expressed by B-cell-activating-FDC [26].
The few studies performed to understand the functions of this protein suggest that it can modulate B-cell immune response [26][27] and may have a role in autoimmune diseases [28][29].

title: PSMC2, ORC5 and KRTDAP are specific biomarkers for HPV-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
summary: Broader-literature context for the second atlas marker, KRTDAP. Describes KRTDAP as a soluble regulator of keratinocyte differentiation with a key role in embryonic skin morphogenesis. Supports the interpretation that the FDCSP epithelium cluster is a differentiated oral-mucosa/keratinocyte-type epithelial population. Study is HNSCC-focused; KRTDAP expression evidence is transcript-level.
quotes: KRTDAP acts as a soluble regulator of keratinocyte differentiation and serves a key role in embryonic skin morphogenesis (44).
